description:
This is inside the Enhanced Games - the competition some have dubbed the "Steroid Olympics".
 
The inaugural games featured dozens of elite athletes using performance-enhancing drugs to try and break world records in track, weightlifting and swimming. 
 
The drugs they use must be legal, and approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA).  
 
But substances like testosterone and human growth hormone - banned by the World Anti-Doping Agency - are not only celebrated, they're encouraged and for sale.

The US President Donald Trump has told the BBC that if he tells Israel’s prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu “to do something, he does it”. 

The president was speaking to the BBC’s North America Editor Sarah Smith in a telephone interview, following the recent new round of hostilities between Israel and Iran. 

Israel had launched attacks on Iran’s capital Tehran on Sunday, in apparent defiance of a demand from the White House to comply with the fragile ceasefire in force since April.  Israel said the action was in retaliation for attacks by the Iranian backed Hezbollah militia group in Southern Lebanon.

Iran responded to the airstrikes by firing multiple missiles at Israel, the first such attack since April.

Hours before Israel launched its attacks, President Trump had declared “I call the shots” and had instructed Benjamin Netanyahu to comply with the ceasefire.

author: BBC News
description:
Multiple women have accused billionaire businessman and West Ham co-owner David Sullivan of abusing his power and preying on them for sex, in some cases when they were in their late teens.

The allegations from seven women have been uncovered in a joint investigation by BBC Panorama and the Times and span decades, starting in the 1980s. All come from women who were in their late teens or early twenties and were young models seeking work at Sullivan's Daily and Sunday Sport newspapers.

They accuse Sullivan of sexually exploitative and predatory behaviour, including pressuring them for sex during business meetings, where he offered to boost their careers if they slept with him or gave him oral sex.

David Sullivan has categorically denied the claims.

If you are affected by some of the issues in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line (https://www.bbc.co.uk/actionline/).

US President Donald Trump appears to be increasingly frustrated with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, analysts say, as Israeli operations against Iran and Hezbollah have threatened Washington's ceasefire with Tehran.

We ask the BBC's Middle East analyst Sebastian Usher what leverage Donald Trump has to ensure Benjamin Netanyahu adheres to a ceasefire, and whether the US-Israel alliance is at risk. 

Iran launched strikes on Israel at the weekend, in retaliation for Israel's campaign against Hezbollah in Lebanon - and Israel fired back at Iran, despite warnings from Mr Trump not to do so. On Monday, the president urged both sides to "stop shooting", and both Iran and Israel agreed - though Mr Netanyahu said Israel would strike Iran with full force if it is attacked by Tehran again.

author: BBC News
description:
Can a company take away something you've already paid for?
 
In the world of online video games, some already do. Publishers can decide to switch off a game's servers, often leaving it effectively unplayable.
 
Stop Killing Games, a growing consumer rights campaign started by American YouTuber Ross Scott in 2024, is challenging that practice.
 
In January, the group submitted a petition featuring nearly 1.3 million signatures to the European Commission, triggering a public hearing in the European Parliament in April. What began as an online campaign is now awaiting a decision from one of the EU's most powerful institutions.
 
Ubisoft has already defended its position in court. Responding to a proposed class-action lawsuit brought by two The Crew players in California, the studio argued that customers had purchased a licence to use the game, not unlimited ownership rights, and that players had been warned online services would not be available forever.

title: Stop Killing Games: Gamers take on the industry to stop games being switched off for good | BBC News

#Philippines #Asia #EarthquakeAt least 32 people have died after a magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck off the coast of Mindanao island in the southern Philippines, officials have said.
 
The quake hit at 07:37 local time on Monday (Sunday 23:37 GMT), triggering tsunami alerts in the Philippines, Indonesia, Japan and Australia. Some of those were cancelled hours later.
 
Videos and images showed buildings collapsing, and landslides have been recorded in some areas.
 
More than 100 people have been injured across several provinces, almost two dozen are missing, and 10,000 residents have been pre-emptively evacuated, authorities have said.

description:
US President Donald Trump tells Israel and Iran to stop "shooting", after the countries attacked each other's territory for the first time since the April ceasefire.
 
Israel carried out air strikes in western and central Iran, after Iran fired missiles at northern Israel.
 
Iran said it's "the beginning of a full week of continuous strikes" - it launched its attacks after Israel carried out air strikes on Beirut in Lebanon on Sunday.
 
The Israeli military said those strikes, on Hezbollah targets in the city's southern suburbs, were a response to Hezbollah firing rockets at Israel.
